articles.title: Mobile science labs improve science results in South Africa
articles.titleCn: 移动科学实验室提升南非科学成绩
articles.summary: South African innovation companies that design and deploy modular and mobile science laboratories for schools are helping learners improve their marks in science.

South Africa's Department of Basic Education has made improving mathematics and physical sciences results a national priority.
The goal is to address shortages of technical and scientific skills in the economy but progress has been slow.
Physical sciences pass rates in the 2025 matric exams edged up only slightly, from 76% to 77%, even as more students enrolled in the subject. Mathematics results, another gateway subject for careers in science and engineering, actually declined over the same period.

"The practical lessons have changed the way many of us think about physical sciences," Mkhize said. "Instead of memorizing theory, we can test what we've learned, and that has helped improve our understanding and our results."
A modular structure built by Kusile Labs & Technology at Pine Ridge Combined School in South Africa's Mpumalanga province, October 22, 2022. /Kusile Labs & Technology
A gap in school infrastructure
Behind the national numbers is a stark infrastructure gap. Department of Basic Education data has repeatedly shown that only about one in five public schools has a science laboratory. Roughly three-quarters lack a library. The shortages are worse in poorer provinces such as Limpopo and the Eastern Cape. Government estimates put the cost of closing school infrastructure gaps nationwide in the tens of billions of rand.
The small national gain in physical sciences came even as enrollment in the subject grew. South Africa's Basic Education Minister, Siviwe Gwarube, has pointed out that the country is seeing growth in learner numbers without a corresponding gain in educational quality.
Teachers say access to laboratory equipment is making a real difference. Velile Njobe, a science teacher at Pine Ridge Combined School in Mpumalanga, says the resources are transforming how students learn.
"Practical work allows learners to connect theory with real-life applications," Njobe said. "We've seen students become more engaged in class, ask better questions and develop greater confidence. Access to a laboratory gives them the opportunity to build the skills that Physical Sciences requires."
At Simanyene High School, Principal Miss Gxagxama has seen a similar shift since a mobile laboratory was installed there in 2018.
"We received a donated mobile lab to the school and now the learners are able to do practicals and not only learn physical sciences through theory and textbook learning. Our school had a non-functioning lab and expired chemicals, now Kusile Labs sends us chemicals annually. Since working with them, our school's results have gradually improved," she said.
At Simanyene High School, physical sciences results have undergone a remarkable transformation. The matric pass rate rose from 37.5% in 2020 to 65.3% in 2021, before climbing above 95% in 2022 and reaching 100% in 2025. Pine Ridge Combined School has followed a similar path, recording steady gains in physical sciences performance since 2022.
Kusile Labs & Technology workers assemble a modular science structure at Pine Ridge Combined School in Mpumalanga, September 2, 2022. /Kusile Labs & Technology
Where the laboratories come from
Kusile Labs & Technology built the laboratories at both schools. The South African company designs modular and mobile units for schools that cannot afford, or do not have space for, conventional laboratories.
According to co-founder Pamella Maseko, the company does not determine which schools benefit from the laboratory projects. That decision is generally made by the corporate sponsors providing the funding.
A school with no room to build gets a mobile laboratory that can be wheeled between classrooms. A school with available land can get a modular unit, assembled on-site from prefabricated parts.
Maseko explained that the process takes only a few weeks, compared with roughly three years for a conventional laboratory. "The modular structure does not necessarily require all the regulatory frameworks that often take so long to implement and fulfill," she added.
Kusile Labs also hires young people from the communities where it builds laboratories, training them to work alongside its own staff during installation, which alleviates unemployment in a country where joblessness among 15- to 24-year-olds reached 60.9% in the first quarter of 2026, according to Statistics South Africa.
Equipment that comes with the science laboratorties seen at Solomon Mahlungu High School in Uitenhage, Eastern Cape, in March 2018. /Kusile Labs & Technology
A larger, unfinished project
Simanyene and Pine Ridge are two examples in a much bigger challenge. Five decades since the Soweto Uprising, access to quality science education remains out of reach for millions of South African learners.
For students like Ndlovu, Sefoloko and Mkhize, that is starting to change. They can now do the experiments themselves, instead of only reading about them.

Wang attended the Meeting of the Council of the Ministers of Foreign Affairs of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Member States in Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan, on Friday and also held bilateral talks with leaders from Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan.
According to China's Foreign Ministry, the discussions focused on strengthening coordination on multilateral platforms and promoting the development of the SCO and the China-Central Asia mechanism.
Kyrgyzstan was recently elected as a nonpermanent member of the United Nations Security Council, and it is set to host the SCO Bishkek Summit later this year.
Kyrgyzstan has joined the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, which was founded earlier this month in Shanghai, as well as the International Organization for Mediation.
During his meeting with Wang on Friday, Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov said that his country is demonstrating through concrete actions its support for the four global initiatives proposed by China — the Global Development Initiative, the Global Security Initiative, the Global Civilization Initiative, and the Global Governance Initiative.
Kyrgyzstan is willing to further strengthen communication and coordination with China within multilateral frameworks, including the UN and the China-Central Asia mechanism, to jointly promote regional and global peace and development, Japarov added.
Wang said that China will, as always, firmly support Kyrgyzstan's independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity.
He also expressed China's readiness to strengthen coordination and cooperation with Kyrgyzstan on UN affairs and to support Kyrgyzstan in successfully hosting the SCO Bishkek Summit.
Liu Shiguo, a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Institute of World Economics and Politics, said that Wang's visit was a journey of friendship, cooperation and peace, adding that "China has always been a trustworthy neighbor, partner and friend to the Central Asian countries".
The Central Asian region is one of the core areas for jointly building the Belt and Road Initiative, and China and Kyrgyzstan "have significant potential for cooperation in emerging fields such as AI-powered social governance, smart agriculture and cross-border data governance", Liu told China Youth Daily.
During his meeting with Uzbek Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov on Thursday, Wang said that China is ready to work with Uzbekistan to promote the high-quality construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan Railway, a major BRI project, and to create more landmark projects in new industrialization.
Saidov said that Uzbekistan opposes any actions undermining China's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and that his country is pleased to join the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization.
Sirojiddin Rahmonov, a senior specialist at the Center for the Study of Transport and Logistics Development Problems under Uzbekistan's Ministry of Transport, said that continued improvements in cross-border infrastructure can help build a robust safeguard against a relapse into poverty.
Uzbekistan will continue to deepen pragmatic and multilateral cooperation with China in areas such as connectivity, trade and investment, and advance regional integration, Rahmonov said at a seminar held this month in Urumqi, Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region.
Tajik President Emomali Rahmon paid a successful visit to China in May. The most important outcome of his visit was the signing of the China-Tajikistan Treaty on Permanent Good-Neighborliness, Friendship and Cooperation, which "set a precedent in Central Asia", Wang said during a meeting on Friday with Tajik Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Muhriddin.

articles.fullText:
As people age, many experience memory decline and slower cognitive processing, along with a higher risk of cerebrovascular disease and cognitive impairment. One important question in aging research is how changes in the brain's blood vessels contribute to cognitive decline.
Scientists from the Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology (SIAT) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have identified a mechanism by which aging weakens the blood-brain barrier, the brain's protective interface with the bloodstream.
The study was published in Neuron under the title "TGF-β1-induced endothelial transcytosis drives blood-brain barrier leakage during aging."
The study shows how aging disrupts transport in brain blood vessel cells, leading to blood-brain barrier leakage. /SIAT
The blood-brain barrier, or BBB, acts as a selective security system. It allows essential nutrients to reach the brain while preventing potentially harmful substances in the blood from entering brain tissue. Damage to this barrier has been linked to cognitive aging, cerebral small vessel disease and several neurodegenerative disorders.
Scientists have traditionally attributed BBB leakage mainly to damage to the tight seals between cells lining brain blood vessels. However, the new study found that another process occurs earlier during aging.
By examining mice at different ages, the researchers found that BBB leakage was already detectable in middle-aged mice and worsened in older animals. The change appeared early in the hippocampus, a brain region important for learning and memory.
At this stage, the seals between blood vessel cells remained largely intact. Instead, the cells' internal transport system became abnormally active, allowing blood-borne substances to pass through the cells and enter brain tissue.
"Rather than first leaking through gaps between cells, the aging blood-brain barrier appears to lose control over transport pathways inside the cells," the researchers said.
The team identified a protein called Mfsd2a as an important part of this protective system. Mfsd2a normally limits unnecessary transport across brain blood vessels. Its levels declined with age, while Caveolin-1, a protein involved in the formation of transport vesicles, increased.
When the researchers restored endothelial Mfsd2a expression or knocked down Caveolin-1 in aged mice, abnormal vesicle transport and BBB leakage were significantly reduced.
The researchers then investigated why Mfsd2a declines during aging. They found that levels of TGF-β1, a signaling molecule involved in inflammation, tissue repair and aging, increased in both the brain and the bloodstream as mice aged.
Excessive TGF-β1 reduced Mfsd2a expression in the cells lining brain blood vessels, causing their transport activity to increase. Raising TGF-β1 levels in young mice caused them to develop several features normally seen in the aged BBB, including increased leakage.
By contrast, blocking TGF-β signaling in aged mice reduced BBB leakage and improved their performance in memory-related behavioral tests.
The findings suggest that age-related BBB damage is not simply the result of passive wear and tear. Instead, it involves biological signals that alter how brain blood vessel cells transport substances.
The study may help explain how vascular changes contribute to cognitive aging. It also points to potential approaches for protecting the aging brain, including maintaining Mfsd2a function or preventing excessive activation of TGF-β signaling. Further research will be needed to determine whether these strategies can be safely translated into treatments for humans.

The 25th China Internet Conference opens at the China National Convention Center in Beijing, capital of China, July 8, 2026. 
Artificial intelligence is moving rapidly from experimental technology to real-world applications, as industry leaders showcased new AI-powered solutions for cities, businesses and consumers at the 25th China Internet Conference in Beijing.
Held from July 8 to 10, the conference highlighted how AI agents, large language models and digital twin technologies are being integrated into sectors ranging from urban governance and industrial manufacturing to retail and public services.
Speaking via video at the opening ceremony, Wu Hequan, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering, said AI-native technologies are reshaping the internet itself.
While large language models excel at general reasoning, AI agents are designed to execute specific tasks and future digital ecosystems will increasingly rely on collaboration among multiple intelligent agents rather than isolated AI systems.
Participants of the 25th China Internet Conference try on VR products at the China National Convention Center in Beijing, capital of China, July 8, 2026. 
According to Wu, AI-generated traffic is expected to account for around 60% of global internet traffic by 2030, with AI agent services becoming the dominant source of token-based interactions. The shift, he said, will require internet infrastructure to evolve toward higher bandwidth, lower latency and stronger computing capabilities.
The conference also demonstrated how AI is being deployed in practical scenarios. Digital assistants are supporting office collaboration and customer services, while AI-powered inspection systems are improving industrial operations. Digital twin technologies are enabling more efficient traffic management, energy optimization and building maintenance, providing city managers with real-time visualization and decision-making tools.
Industry representatives also emphasized that AI innovation is creating measurable economic value.
Participants of the 25th China Internet Conference interact with humanoid robots at the China National Convention Center in Beijing, capital of China, July 8, 2026. 
At the conference, Kuaishou said its AI-powered video generation model and digital human live-streaming platform have helped small and medium-sized businesses increase daily gross merchandise value while significantly reducing marketing costs. Alibaba's Taobao Instant Commerce platform reported that AI agents are increasingly handling complex shopping requests, moving beyond traditional keyword-based searches to task-oriented consumer services.
Beyond applications, participants identified trustworthy AI and green computing as key priorities for the industry's next stage of development. The launch of the FlagOS Initiative, an open AI software platform designed to improve compatibility across different computing chips, reflects broader efforts to build more efficient and sustainable AI infrastructure.
As AI technologies continue to mature, industry experts believe the focus is shifting from developing models to deploying them at scale. The conference highlighted China's efforts to accelerate AI adoption across the real economy, with intelligent applications increasingly becoming part of everyday life while supporting digital transformation and high-quality economic development.
